ORDINANCE NO. 348.

AN ORDINANCE granting J. Downey Harvey, E. L. Stern, H. W. O’Melveny and
Daniel Freeman and their assigns the right to erect poles and run wires
along the public streets of the City of Los Angeles, and to establish and
maintain a district telegraph company for a period of twenty-five years.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows :

Section 1. J. Downey Harvey, E. L. Stern, H. W. O’Melveny and Daniel
Freeman are hereby granted, for the period of twenty-five years from the date of
the passage and approyal of this ordinance, the rignt, and are hereby authorized,
to erect and maintain telegraph poles upon, and to run wires over and along, the
public streets and thoroughfares within the limits of the City of Los Angeles,
under the provisions of Sections 2 and 3 of this ordinance; provided that the
=== p-124 ===
120 ORDINANCES OF THE

 

said J. Downey Harvey et al., or their assigns, pay into the City Treasury of said
city such license fee as may now be in force or hereafter passed by proper ordi-
nance for the privilege of carrying on said business.

Src. 2. Such poles so erected and to be erected shall be placed fifty yards
apart, unless otherwise ordered by the Council of said city, or by the successors in
interest and right of said Council, and shall in all cases set in and be flush with

: the face of the curb, where streets are sidewalked, when not otherwise directed
by the said Council, or its suecessors, and upon all the other streets and thorough-
fares at such points as may be designated by said Council or its successors ; pro

vided that the said Harvey et al., or their assigns, shall use no poles in the
construction and maintenance of said district telegraph system within the fol-
lowing limits of Los Angeles City, unless Ly permission of the City Council
thereunto obtained, ‘to-wit: Within a circle whose radius is one mile, taking the
Plaza as a center. The Council of the City of Los Angeles and its said sue-
cessors shall have supervision over and determine the location, under this ordi-
nance, of all poles to be erected by said Harvey et al., or their assigns. Said
Council, for itself and its successors, reserves the right to remove or cause to be
removed any of the poles or wires of said Harvey et al., or their assigns, when-
ever the Council shall require the removal of the same elsewhere. In no case
shall any wire of said Harvey et al., or their assigns, be lower than eighteen feet
from the ground, and the said wires shall be entirely above or below the other
telephone and telegraph wires in said City, and in no case shall the wires of
Harvey et al. be within six feet of the city fire alarm system. The said district
telegraph system shall be in working order within ninety days from the taking
effect of this ordinance.

Sec. 3. Said Harvey et al., and their assigns, shall give, during all the
period of said twenty-five years, free of charge to the City of Los Angeles, the
use of all their lines and wires within the limits of said city for the Police and
Fire Departments, and all other city officials, for the transaction of the public
business, and shal! immediately place and, during all of said period of twenty-five —
years, shall maintain a box as is used in said system in the city office of the City
Auditor, Chief of Police of said city, and in every room in which any fire engine,
hose cart or hook and ladder truck belonging to said city shall be stationed.

Sec. 4. This franchise is granted upon each and every condition contained
in this ordinance; and upon the failure or refusal of said Harvey et al., or their
assigns, to comply with any one or more of the conditions of this ordinance, this
franchise shall at once cease and determine, and the said Harvey et al., and their
assigns, shall have no rights whatever by virtue of this ordinance,

Sec. 5. Nothing herein contained shall be construed as granting an exclusive
franchise or creating a monopoly of said business, and the said Harvey et al.
shall, within twenty days, file with the City Clerk an acceptance of this franchise.
=== p-125 ===

ordinance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles
Daily Tribune, a newspaper published in said city, and thereupon and thereafter”
it shall take effect and be in force.

J hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of

ORDINANCE NO. 350.

An ORDINANCE amending an ordinance granting to Edward Records and C. J.
Richards a franchise for the construction of a street railroad in the City of
Los Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

That the following amendment be inserted in Section 1 of Ordinance No.
311, viz: After the words “drawn or propelled by’ be inserted the words “ horses
or mules,” and after the words “ over the entire route” be inserted the following:
“ And if horses or mules be used, two horses or two mules shall draw each car;
and furthermore, the use of horses or mules is granted for one year only, and upon
condition that said grantees or assigns shall commence work on said road within
sixty days from the date of the taking effect of this amendment, and be completed
within ninety days after commencement, and that cars on said road shall be run
at intervals of not more than ten minutes,” so that Section 1 of said ordinance
shall read as follows:

Section 1. That the right of way be and the same is hereby granted to
Edward Records and C. J. Richards and assigns over and along the public streets
of said city hereinafter named for the period of thirty years from and after the
date of the taking effect of this ordinance, for the purpose of making all necessary
excavations, constructing, laying down, maintaining and operating a single (or
double) track street railroad, with iron or steel rails, and necessary turnouts or
switches, the cars thereof to be drawn or propelled by horses or mules, electric or
cable power ; and if electric power be used no poles are to be erected on the streets
or sidewalks; and should cable power be used the slot in the center of the track
shall not exceed seven-eighths of an inch over the entire route; and if horses or
mules be used, two horses or two mules shall draw each car; and furthermore, the
use of horses or mules is granted for one year only, and upon condition that said
=== p-128 ===
124 ORDINANCES OF THE

grantees or assigns shall commence work on said road within sixty days from the
date of the taking effect of this amendment, and be completed within ninety days after
conimencement, and that cars on said road shall be run at intervals of not more
than ten minutes, viz: Commencing at the intersection of Mission road with
Macy street, thence along Mission road to its intersection with Griffin avenue,
thence along Griffin avenue to its intersection with Patrick street; provided and
on condition that the said grantees, or their successors, or assigns, shall plank,
pave or macadamize the whole of said road between the rails and for two feet on
each side thereof, and provide it for its entire length with wooden stringers not
less than four inches wide, spiked to the ties against the outside of and up to and
flush with the top of the rail, and shall keep the same constantly in repair, flush
with the grade of the street, and provided with good crossings for all kinds of
vehicles, and with all necessary and proper flumes for the free passage of water
under said track, and that there be sufficient space between the tracks and side-
tracks or turnouts to allow the cars of said road to pass each other freely and
without danger; and that the width of said track shall not be greater than 4 feet
83 inches between the rails; and provided, further, that the roadbed and track
shall conform in all cases where a grade has been established to such grade,
and in all other cases to the natural grade of the streets through which they
run, and when at any time the whole ur any part of said route shall be either,
graded, paved or otherwise improved, or the grade or improvements thereof
changed or altered, the bed of the road and the track thereof shall be, by the
grantees or assignees, made to conform, in grade or material, or both, therewith ;
and provided, further, that no turnouts or switches shall be constructed in places
other than those designated by the said City Council or its successors, which
authority shall also prescribe the radii of curves to be used in swinging the line of
said road from one street to another; and provided, further, that whenever the
grading of the trackbed makes the street impassable for traffic, the grantees or

but one-half of said fare on any of its cars from or to said schools; provided said
pupils shall purchase their fares in quantities of not less than one dollar’s worth
at a time, and said grantees or assigns shall transfer passengers without extra
charge over their line between the Plaza and the eastern limits of the city from
the junction of Mission road, and also over any railroads that they may hereafter
build or acquire; and provided, further, that the grantees or assigns of said road
shall, on or before the 15th day of December of each year pay to said city such
license fee upon each car as may be required by the ordinances of said city; and
provided, further, that if at any time for the space of one month the.said road
or any portion thereof shall be unused as a street railroad the franchise for the
portions so unused shall be thereby forfeited.

ORDINANCE NO. 352.

AN ORDINANCE granting permission and authority to Hervey Lindley to erect
buildings for storing natural gas, and to store such gas therein, and to lay
pipes for the conducting such gas through the streets, avenues, alleys and
public ground of said city.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. There is hereby granted to Hervey Lindley, his successors and
assigns, permission and authority, by the consent of the City Council of the City
of Los Angeles first obtained, to erect such buildings and machinery within the
corporate limits of said city (not to be erected in any street or on any other public
ground) as may be necessary for procuring and storing natural gas, to be used for
the purpose of furnishing and selling said natural gas as a fuel in any buildings,
manufactories or houses in the form of natural gas, and to have the right to lay
pipes for the purpose of conducting such gas in any of the streets, avenues, lanes,
alleys and public grounds of said city, and to furnish said gas to any inhabitant
of said city.
=== p-132 ===
128 ORDINANCES OF THE

Sxc. 2. Saidecompany shall lay said pipes under the surface of said streets, »
avenues, alleys, lanes and squares of said city, and to conform to the grades,
established therein and at such depth as may be necessary to protect the same,
and on condition that it shall cause the surface of. such ayenue, street, alley,
lane or public ground to be restored to the condition in which it was prior to_
laying the’same; and should the grade of any street be lowered, said company
shall lower its pipes, when notified so to do by said city, at its own cost and
expense, and the laying of pipes and mains in the streets, shall be under the
direction of the City Engineer, and shall be done in accordance with any ordinance,
of said city now or hereafter passed.

Said company shall at all times protect, defend and save harmless the City of
Los Angeles from any and all damages, from any and all actions at law, by per-
sons or property being injured by the improper or negligent manner of using said
streets for the conveyance of said gas, and shall always protect by proper barricade
and light all excavations which may be made for such purpose.

Src. 3. Said company, its successors and assigns, shall be entitled to enjoy
all privileges granted hereby and conferred for the period of fifty years from and
after the passage of this ordinance. If said works are not in successful operation
by January 1, 1892, then the rights herein granted shall be null and void; pro-
vided, however, that in computing time herein no portion thereof during which
said company is by legal injunction or restraining order of court prevented from
prosecuting said work shall be included.

Sec. 4. All the rights herein granted are subject to the rights heretofore
vested in any other corporation, and the City of Los Angeles in no wise warrants
any of the rights or privileges herein granted, and. said city is not to be subject
to any claims for damage on account of anything herein contained.

Sec. 5. The City Council reserves the right to regulate and require the
carrying of said natural gas through the streets and public grounds of said city
and into the buildings thereof by such ordinances as may be reasonable and.
proper. ;

Sec. 6. Within thirty days after the approval of this ordinance said Lindley
shall file in the office of the City Clerk of the City of Los Angeles his written
acceptance of the provisions of this ordinance, if said Lindley desires to avail
himself of the benefits thereof. Unless such acceptance is so filed, the provisions _
hereof shall not be binding, and the rights herein granted shall be forfeited.

City of Los Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. It shall be unlawful, except in such cases as are hereinafter pro-
=== p-148 ===
144 ORDINANCES OF TH#H

vided, to hitch any horse, mule or any other beast of draft or burden, or leave
standing, not in the immediate care of some person, any carriage, buggy, wagon,
cart or other vehicle, with or without animals attached, upon any of the follows
ing named public streets of the City of Los Angeles, between the hours of 8
o'clock a. m.and 6 o'clock p.m. on all days of the year except Sunday, viz:
On Spring street, from Fourth street to Temple street; on Main street, from
Fourth street to Marchessault street; on Second street, from Los Angeles street
to Fort street; on First street, from Fort street to Alameda street ; on Franklin,
Court, Market, Commercial, Arcadia and Sonora streets; on Requena street,
from Main street to Los Angeles street; on Temple street, from Spring street to
New High street.

Health Officer, the Street Superintendent, the Chief and all officers of the Police
Department of the city, when in discharge of their duties as such, all merchants,
while receiving and delivering goods, and all practicing physicians shall be
exempt from any penalty by the violation of this ordinance.

Sec. 3. Any person violating any of the provisions of this ordinance shall
be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be punished by imprisonment in
the county jail for a period not exceeding sixty days, or by fine not exceeding
two hundred dollars, or by both such fine and imprisonment.

they conflict with this ordinance, shall be, and the same are hereby repealed.

nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Tribune, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take eflect and be in force.

ORDINANCE NO. 372.
Ay ORDINANCE regulating the carrying of deadly or dangerous weapons.
The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

‘Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any persons excepting peace officers or
persons actually traveling through said city to wear or carry upon their persons
any dirk, bowie-knife, sword-cane, pistol, revolver, or any other dangerous or
deadly weapon, within the corporate limits of the City of Los Angeles, without a
duly issued permit.

 

Sxc. 2. Permits to carry weapons may be issued by the Police Commission,
or a majority of them, to such persons as in their best judgment should have that
- privilege.

<
=== p-156 ===
152 ’ ORDINANCES OF THE

Src. 3. Any person who shall wear or carry upon his person any of the above —
mentioned weapons, or any dangerous or deadly weapon, shall be deemed guilty of
a misdemeanor, and upon conviction thereof, shall be fined not to exceed two hun-
dred dollars, or shall be imprisoned in the City Jail not to exceed ninety days. a

Sec. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify: to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Evening Express,
and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of %
the City of Los Angeles at its meeting of January 3, 1888. oe

out his approval on the 3d day of February, 1888. By reason of not being re-
turned within fifteen days (Sundays and other legal holidays excepted), the said
ordinance has become effective and as valid as if the Mayor had approved and
signed it.

FREEMAN G. TEED,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Published February 4, 1888.

ORDINANCE NO. 377.

Aw Orprxance prohibiting the erection of certain buildings in certain limits in
the City of Los Angeles.

_ The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows :

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation to erect

any livery stable, powder-house, stone crusher, rolling mill, liquor store, saloon,

_ soap factory, gas works, bowling alley or dance house outside the limits of Fire

District No. 1 of the general fire limits of the City of Los Angeles, and within

the corporate limits of said city, without a permit from the Mayor so to do,

which permit shall be granted only upon the petition of three-fourths of the
property owners in the block in which said building is proposed to be erected.

Sec. 2. Any person who shall violate the provisions of this ordinance shall
be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction thereof, shall be fined
not to exceed two hundred dollars, or shall be imprisoned not to exceed ninety
days, or shall suffer both said fine and imprisonment in the discretion of the court.

Sec. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Evening
Express, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Couacil of
the City of Los Angeles at its meeting of February 27, 1888.

FREEMAN G. TEED,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

ORDINANCE NO. 403.
Aw ORDINANCE forbidding blasting within the limits of the City of Los Angeles
The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows :

Section 1, That it shall be unlawful for any person to blast any rock or
other substance, or to use any dynamite, giant powder, nitro-glycerine, or any
other explosive, for blasting purposes, within the corporate limits of the City of
Los Angeles, without a permit from the Police Commissioners; and said permit
shall not be granted until the parties applying for the same shall present a good
and sufficient bond for the indemnifying of any property owners against any loss
of property that might ensue by reason of said blasting.

Sec. 2. Any person who shall violate a provision of this ordinance shall be
deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and upon conviction thereof shall be fined not
to exceed three hundred dollars, or shall be imprisoned not to exceed two hundred
days, or shall suffer both fine and imprisonment.

Sere. 3, The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
Nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Evening

Express, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

ORDINANCE NO. 408.

Aw ORDINANCE regulating the disposal of dead animals in the City of Los
Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any person or persons to allow the dead
bodies of any horses, mules, cattle, goats, sheep or hogs, which shall die in their
possession, to remain unburied for the space of four hours without reporting the
death of said animal to the Chief of Police at his office.

Sec. 2. Every person in whose possession, any horse, mule, cow, ox, steer,
calf, goat, sheep or hog shall die, shall bury said animal, as provided in the ordi-
nances of said city, within four hours after its death, or shall report the death of —
said animal as above provided, and shall leave with the Chief of Police a fee of —

six dollars to pay the expense of removing the carcass from the city limits and
disposing of the same.

Src. 3. Any person who shall violate this provision of this ordinance shall _
be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and upon conviction thereof shall be fined not
exceeding two hundred dollars, or shall be imprisoned not to exceed one hundred _
days, or suffer both fine and imprisonment.

Src. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Evening Express,
and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

ORDINANCE NO, 411.

Ayn ORDINANCE declaring and determining the necessity for a certain public
improvement of a permanent character by the construction of an outfall
sewer, in connection with ‘the general sewerage system of the City of Los
Angeles.

_ The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

_ Secrion 1. That the public interest and necessity demand the acquisition
of the right of way over and upon certain lands lying between the south charter
boundary of the City of Los Angeles and a point on the beach of the Pacific
Ocean, for the purpose of the construction of an outfall sewer for the sewer sys-
tem of the City of Los Angeles; and that the further public interest and necessity
demand the laying and construction of said outfall sewer over and along said
route, which route is more fully described as follows:

Commencing at the junction of San Pedro street with the south city boun-
dary; thence running along Jefferson street, size 2 feet by 3 feet, 2,460 feet to
Santa Monica Railroad right of way at Main street; thence running parallel
With said railroad and about 20 feet from same to Grand avenue, 2 feet by 3
feet, 1,400 feet ; thence along said railroad to west city line, 3 feet 4 inches by 5
feet, 2,100 feet ; thence along same railroad to a point 1,500 feet south of Cienega
Station, 2 feet 8 inches by 4 feet, 14,800 feet; thence along same railroad to a
point 7,000 feet north of Ballona creek crossing on railroad, 3 feet by 4 feet 6
inches, 7,000 feet; thence along same railroad to Ballona creek crossing of rail-
road, 3 feet 4 inches by 5 feet, 7,000 feet; thence along same railroad to county

+ oad running to South Santa Monica, 3 feet 4 inches by 5 feet, 2,700 feet ; thence
13 :
=== p-203 ===
198 ORDINANCES OF THE

along county road, 3 feet 4 inches by 5 feet, 5,000 feet; thence along same road,
2 feet 8 inches by 4 feet, 5,000 feet ; thence along same road, 3 feet 2 inches by 4
feet 9 inches, 12,000 feet ; thence across country toward the ocean, 3 feet 4 inches
by 5 feet, 7,500 feet; thence to ocean beach at a point about two miles southeast
of the Arcadia Hotel at Santa Monica, 3 feet 9 inches, round.

The total distance from San Pedro street is 70,460 feet, and the distance from
west city line to the ocean beach is 64,500 feet, or twelve and twenty-one hun-

dredths (12.21) miles.

The work to consist of excavation for and the laying of these conduits with
brick or broken stone concrete, or with both, as the Council may determine,
together with about thirty manholes and such gates as may be found necessary
during construction to accommodate the residents along the line who may desire
to use the sewerage, and also for bridging or other means of crossing the Ballona

ereek and for work at output.

The estimated cost of the above mentioned improvements is three hundred
and fifty thousand dollars, and that the debt proposed to be incurred is for the
purpose of paying the cost of the same, and that the cost of said improvements
is too great to be paid out of the ordinary annual income and revenue of the
municipality.

Sec. 2. That said improvement is of a permanent municipal character and
that the City of Los Angeles shall proceed to provide for the necessity set forth
in Section 1 of this ordinance, and to pay the cost and expense of the acquisition |
of the right of way and of the laying and constructing of said outfall sewer, by
the issue of permanent municipal improvement bonds of the City of Los
Angeles. Said Council shall proceed to incur such indebtedness according to the -
provisions of an act authorizing the incurring of indebtedness by cities, towns
and municipal corporations incorporated under the laws of the State of Califor-
nia, approved March 15, A. D., 1887.

Sec. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance by a vote of three-fourths of all the members of the Council of the City
of Los Angeles, and shall cause the same, when approved by the Mayor of the
city, to be published daily for two weeks in the Los Angeles Daily Evening
Express, and thereupon and thereafter it shall be in full effect and foree.

held August 27, 1888, twelve members of said Council voted in fayor
of the adoption of said ordinance, as will more fully appear by the records of

ORDINANCE NO. 416.

AN ORDINANCE granting to the Mateo Street and Santa Fe Avenue Street Car
Company a franchise for the construction and operation of a street railway in
the City of Los Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. That the franchise and right of way be and the same is hereby

 
=== p-208 ===
 

 

CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 203

granted to the Mateo Street and Santa Fe Avenue Street Car Company, a corpora~
tion, and its assigns, over and along the following streets in the City of Los
Angeles, for the period of thirty years from the date this ordinance takes effect,
for the purpose of laying, maintaining and operating one line of iron street rail-
way, with two parallel rails distant from each other at least 3 feet 6 inches; and
to run its cars thereon, to be drawn or propelled by two horses or mules, and to
carry passengers in its cars thereon, with the privilege of constructing necessary
turntables and sidetracks ; that is to say; Commencing on Santa Fe avenue, opposite
the north end of the passenger depot of the California Central Railroad; thence
on said avenue to Second street; thence on Second street to Rio street ; thence on
Rio street to Third street; thence on Third street to Mateo street; thence on
Mateo street to Palmetto street ; thence on Palmetto street to Mateo street ; thence
on Mateo street to and across Seventh street to Legrand street ; thence on Legrand
street to Santa Fe ayenue ; thence on Santa Fe avenue to the charter boundary of
the City of Los Angeles. The sidetracks and turntables shall be placed at such
points as the Council may direct and under the direction of the Superintendent of
Streets.

Src, 2. The laying of said track shall be completed within four months
after this ordinance takes effect.

Sec. 3. The laying of said track shall conform to the established grade of
the streets over which it passed, when the grade has been established, and where
no grade is established, to the natural grade of such streets; and when at any time
any part of said route shall be graded or the grade thereof changed or altered,
the bed of the road and the track thereof shall be made to conform thereto, the
work thereof to be at its own expense.

Sec. 4. Provided and upon condition that the said grantee or its assigns
shall plank, pave or macadamize the entire length of the route along which said
road shall be constructed, between the rails and for two feet on each side thereof
and between the double tracks, whenever the Council of said City of Los Angeles
shall order such streets over which said road may run to be planked, paved, or
macadamized, and that the track ‘shall be paved with the same material as the
balance of the street, and shall keep the same constantly in repair and flush with
the grade of the street.

Sec. 5. Provided, further, that the Superintendent of Streets (or others
having the authority) is hereby authorized to make, levy and collect assessments
for paving and grading against the said railroad, and upon the stock and super-
structure of said road, the same as against private property, for the widths of its
tracks and two feet on each side thereof, except such work that may have hereto-
fore been done to the satisfaction of the Superintendent of Streets and the City
Surveyor of the City of Los Angeles.

Sec. 6. And provided, further, that the grantee or assigns of said road shall,
=== p-209 ===

fee upon each car as may be required by the ordinances of said city; and pro-
vided, further, that if at any time for the space of three months the said road, or
any portion thereof, shall be unused as a street railroad, the franchise for the
portions so unused shall be thereby forfeited.

~

Src. 7. The fare to be charged on said railway is not to exceed 5 cents ; and
provided, further, that persons that attend the public schools of 'the said city as

way and franchisé, expressly reserves the right to grade, sewer, pave, macadamize,

San Gabriel Valley Rapid Transit Railway, and assigns, across the city lands and

years: Commencing at a point on Wabash avenue, 300 feet east of Safford street,
in said City of Los Angeles, at a point north of block 18 of the Brooklyn tract ;
thence across Safford, Lord, Echandia and Gillette streets, in a southerly direction,
across Macy street ; thence in a westerly direction, above grade at street crossings
at least eighteen feet, over and across Anderson street, the Los Angeles river,
Keller street, Center street, Howard street and the Aliso road and Alameda street

to Los Angeles street, at a point 140 feet north of Aliso street; also from a point
on said above described line, beginning at about 500 feet north of Macy street ;*

thence at least eighteen feet under the established grade of Macy strect, Aliso
street and Summit avenue to Rio avenue, and thence southerly over and along
Rio avenue to a point 100 feet north of the north line of First street; also to
connect the last with the first above described line, beginning at a point on
Anderson street, above grade ; running thence on a curved line in a southwesterly
direction, at least twenty feet above, over and across Aliso street and Summit
avenue, to an intersection with the last above described line of said railroad, for
the purpose of making all necessary excavations, constructing, maintaining and
operating a double-track railroad, as indicated on a profile of said road filed in
the office of the Clerk of the Council of said city; provided that the elevation of
said roadway shall, on Alameda street, leave a clear way between its lowest girder
or truss and the official grade of said Alameda street of not less than twenty feet,

upon which the line of said road is definitely located and designated as such by
the blue line shown on said map, and which map is made a part of this descrip-
tion, and shall control the same; and further provided that the entire super-
structure, where crossing streets above grade, shall be of iron (the plans and
specifications to be approved by the Council), and supported by iron columns not
less than six inches in diameter, securely set in the ground with cement footings
(as prescribed by the Council), and it shall pave, as directed by ordinance of the
Council, the entire road bed of all streets over and across which its elevated
structure shall be constructed, from a line running parallel and ten feet distant
outward from a line formed by the iron columns herein mentioned ; and especially
provided that in construction of that portion of the roadway to be elevated above
the surface of the street, plans and specifications shall be filed with the Clerk of
the Council and accepted by the Council, and that until such acceptance of the

crossed at grade between the tracks and rails, and for two feet on each side thereof,

and proper flumes for the free passage of water under said track, and that there be

other freely and without danger; and that the width of said track shall not be

conform, in all cases where a grade has been established, to such grade, and in

_ least twenty-five cents’ worth at a time; and said grantee or assigns shall provide

shall, on or before the 15th day of December of each year, pay to said city such
license fee upon each car as may be required by the ordinances of said city; and
provided, further, that if at any time, for the space of three months, the said road,
or any portion thereof, shall be unused as a railroad, the franchise for the portions
so unused shall be forfeited; and provided, further, that no locomotive or train
shall be allowed to stop on any street crossing, and there shall be no switching on
Rio street.

to use and control all its public streets for any and all purposes, the same as if
_ Ro such franchise existed ; such use to be made so as to obstruct or injure said road

as little as possible; and when work upon, or other use of said streets makes the

expense, so as to avoid the obstructions made thereby; and unless due diligence is
used in the prosecution of said change, the City Superintendent of Streets shall
make said change at the expense of the company.

Src. 3. The above rights and privileges are granted upon the express con-
dition that the said road shall be commenced and completely equipped and in
full running order and operation within two years from the date of the taking
effect of this ordinance, and any failure to complete said road within the time

that case, all rights under this ordinance shall thereupon and immediately be for-
feited, and this grant shall thereupon be null and void; and nothing herein
contained shall be construed as granting an exclusive franchise.

Wherever in this ordinance it mentions the grade of the street or avenue
either as on the grade, or so many feet below or above the grade, it is expressly
understood that the official grade as established by said Council and defined by the
City Surveyor shall be the grade intended in this ordinance, and in any subsequent
change of said grade by said Council the said road shall be made to conform
thereto as required in this ordinance.

But any other new line of railroad or roads shall have the privilege of the
joint use of all said tracks built by said San Gabriel Valley Rapid Transit Rail-
way, its successors or assigns, and on the lands hereby granted said railway by
the city, or over any other lands over which they run in said city, upon paying
their proportion of the costs of all right of way, construction, improvements and
maintenance with one per cent. per month for the said amounts from the date of
this franchise.

Said company by its acceptance of this franchise agrees as follows: That it
will place its tracks upon the official grades of the streets that it crosses and occu-
pies ; that it will raise or lower its road to any modifications of the grades of any

said road at any point within the corporate limits of said city as may be required

making of gravel streets,

owners along said street, amounting to two-thirds of the frontage thereof, shall file wit!

RESOLUTION NO. 570.

A RESOLUTION directing and authorizing the Clerk of the Council to publish notice of
the election to be held on Saturday, the 27th day of August, 1887.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

SEcTION 1, That the Clerk of the Council be and is hereby authorized and directed to
publish, for not less than two weeks, in each of the newspapers of the City of Los
Angeles the following notice of the election to be held in said city on Saturday, the 27th
day of August. 1887, at which election is to be determined by the qualified electors of
said city whether the said City of Los Angeles shall incur an indebtedness of one hun-
dred and fifty thousand dollars, for the purposes set forth in Ordinance No. 329, approved
the 26th day of July, 1887.

ELECTION NOTICE.

Notice is hereby given that a special election of the qualified electors of the eity of
Los Angeles shall be held on Saturday, ‘he 27th day of August, A. D. 1887, under and by
virtue of an ordinance of said city, passed July 25, 1887, and approved July 26, 1887, for
the —— of determining whether said city shall incur a bonded indebtedness of one
hundred and fifty thousand dollars for the purposes in said ordinance set forth, and par-
ticularly described as follows:

The addition of one room to the Highland View school building, in District No. 1.

. icog erection of a new four-room school building on Brooklyn Heights, in District
0.

The alteration of existing rooms and ‘addition of several new ones to the Amelia-
street school building, in District No. 7.

The alterations of existing rooms and addition of several new ones to the Castelar-
street building, in District No. 10.

The erection of a new school building on Pearl street, in District No, 13.
The erection of a new school building on Montgomery street, in District No. 17.
The erection of a new school building on San Pedro street, in District No. 19.

The erection of a new school building at the corner of Fourth and Los Angeles streets,
District No. 20.

oo ne of a site for and erection of a school building on Ninth street, Dis-
0.

The purchasing of a site for and erection of a school building on Diamond street,
District No. 22.

The purchasing of a site for a school building near the corner of Wabash avenue and
Soto street, District No. 23.

The bonds to be issued for the payment of said improvements shall be of the denom-
ination of one thousand dollars each, and of the character known as serials, and one-
twentieth part of the wholeissue shall be payable each and every year, on a day to be
fixed by the Council, and shall bear interest at the rate of five per cent. per annum.

The Council shall, at the time of fixing the general tax levy of said city, and in the
manner for said general tax levy provided, levy and collect annually each year for the
term of twenty years a tax sufficient to pay the annual interest on said bonds, and also
one-twentieth part of the aggregate amount of said indebtedness, as incurred.

The polling places for said election shall be as follows:
For the First Ward—The Southern Hotel, San Fernando street.

For the Second Ward—Supervisor’s Room, Court House.

according to plans and specifications on file in the office of the City surveyor, for the
making of gravel streets.

Sec.2. The Clerk of the Council shall publish a notice of this proceeding each day
for ten consecutive days after the publication of this resolution in the official news-
paper of the city, and if within cen days after the publication of said notice the property
owners along said street, amounting to two-thirds of the frontage thereof, shall file with
the Clerk a written remonstrance against said improvement, then and in that case said
improvement shall not be proceeded with.

SEc.3. The assessment to be levied for the collection of the amount necessary
to pay the cost and expense of improving and grading said street shall be made upon
oy on both sides of said Second street, from its intersection with Figueroa street

the intersection with Pearl street.

Sec. 4. If no remonstrance be filed, as hereinbefore provided, within the time
specified, the Clerk of the Council shall, at the expiration of said time, advertise for
sealed proposals to grade and improve said street in accordance with the said plans and
specifications, and shall return all bids received by him to the Council, and if any bid
be accepted by said Council, the work shall be proceeded with as required by law.

Sec. 5. ‘The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolution, and
shall cause the same to be ena once in the Los Angeles Daily Tribune, and there-
upon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

the law of said State of California and in violation of the provisions and conditions
of the ordinance of the City of Los Angeles; now, therefore,

street railroad in a position that will conform to the requirements and conditions im

Serate and Assembly, did, by an act approved February 28, A. D. 1876, enact a law en-

of said act, the sum of eleven thousand thirty-four and eighty-five hundredths dollars

of central avenue, from Eighth street to Vejar street, and from Washington street
to Alexander avenue.

Section 1. That the grade of Central avenue, from Eighth street to Vejar street
and from Washington street to Alexander avenue, be and the same is hereby established
as follows: At the south line of Eighth street the grade shall be as now established, 17
feet below the datum plane; at the north line of Ninth street the grade shall be 19.07 feet
below the datum plane, and at the south line of said street the grade shall be 19.39 feet
below the datum plane; atthe north line of Twelfth street the grade shall be 22.40 feet
below the datum plane, and at the south line the grade shall be 22.80 feet below the datum
plane; at the northwest corner of Pico street and at a pointin the east line of Central
avenue, opposite said northwest corner of Pico street, the grade shall be 23.50 feet below
the datum plane; at the southwest corner of Pico street and at a point in the east line of
Central avenue, opposite said southwest corner of Pico street, the grade shall be 23.90
feet below the datum plane; at the north line of Vejar street the grade shall be as now
established, 26.50 feet below the datum plane; at a point in the east line of Central
avenue opposite the northwest corner of Washington street the grade shall be 33.50 feet
below the datum plane, and ata point in the east line of Central avenue opposite the
southwest corner of Washington street the grade shall be 34 feet below the datum plane;
at the southwest corner of Washington street the grade shall be as now estahlished, 34
feet below the datum plane; atthe northeast corner of Washington street the grade shall
be 36 feet below the datum pene. and dt a pointin the west line of Central avenue
opposite the northeast corner oi Washington street the grade shall be 36 feet below the
datum plane; ai the southeast corner of Washington street, and at a point in the west
line of Central avenue opposite the southeast corner of Washington street, the grade

(1) That said Sichel street, in said city, from the north line of Mission Road to the
south line of Sigler street, be graded, graveled and curbed, in accordance with plans

» and specifications on file in the office of the Clerk of the Council of the City of Los
Angeles, for making gravel streets in said city,

avenue, from the south line of Diamond street to the north line of Orange street, in

dred feet apart. and if within ten days after the publication of said notice the property

specified, the Council shall have jurisdiction to order said work proceeded with, and to
order Pee street to be graded, graveled and curbed in accordance with said plans and
specifications.

oon of the City of Los Angeles the proposed new Charter for the City of Los

RESOLUTION NO. 856.
RESOLUTION OF INTENTION,

A RESOLUTION of the Mayor and Council of the City ot Los Angeles of their intention to
improve a portion of Adams street.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

SEcTION 1. That the public interest and convenience require that Adams street, in
said city, between Main street and Figueroa street, and including all intersections of
streets, be graded, graveled and curbed; that it is the intention of the Council of said
City of Los Angeles to order the following work to be done, to-wit:

(1) That said Adams street,in said city, from the west line of Main street to the
east line of Figueroa street, be graded, graveled and curbed in accordance with plans
and specifications on file in the office of the Clerk of the Council of the City of Los
Angeles, for making gravel streets in said city.

(2) That a redwood curb be constructed along the line of roadway of said Adams
street, from the west line of Main street to the east line of Figueroa street, in accord-
ance with plans and specifications on file in the office of the Clerk of the Council of
said city, for constructing redwood curbs.

Sec. 2. The Superintendent of Streets shall publish a notice of this proceeding each
day for five consecutive days after the publication of this resolution, in the Los Angeles
Evening Express, the official newspaper of the city, and shall post copies of said notice
along the line of said proposed improvement at a distance not to exceed three hundred
feet apart, and if within ten days after the publication of said notice the property owners
along said street, amounting to one-half of the frontage thereof, shall file with the
Clerk a written objection against said improvement, then and in that case said
improvement shall not be proceeded with.

Sec. 3. If no remonstrance be filed, as hereinbefore provided, within the time
specified, the Council shall have jurisdiction to order said work proceeded with, and to
order said street to be graded, graveled and curbed in accordance with said plans and
specifications.

Sec. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolution, and
cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Evening Express, and there
upon and thereafter it snall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council of the City
of Los Angeles at its meeting of April 23, A. D. 1838, by the following vote:

Ayes—Messrs. Barrett, Book, Chandler, Cohn, Collins, Gibbs, Hanley, Hiller, Lovell,
Mathews, Moriarty, Sinsabaugh Teed and President Humphreys.

Noes—None.
FREEMAN G. TEED,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles,

Approved this 27th day of April, 1888.
W. H. WORKMAN,

; Mayor.

RESOLUTION NO. 976.
‘RESOLUTION OF INTENTION.

A ResoLuTIon of the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles of their intention to
improve a portion of Second street.

Be it resoived by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

SECTION 1, That the public interest and convenience require that Second street, in
said city, between Los Angeles street and Fort street, and including all intersections of
streets, be paved and curbed; that it is the intention of the Council of said City of Los
Angeles to order the following work to be done, to-wit:

(1) That said Second street, in said city, from the west line of Los Angeles street to
the east line of Fort street, be paved with bituminous lime rock in accordance with
oo and specifications on file in the office of the Clerk of the Council of the City of

os Angeles, for paving streets in said city with hydraulic cement and broken stone con-
erete base, with natural bituminous lime rock surface. :

(2) That a granite curb be constructed along the line of roadway of said Second
street, from the west line of Main street to the east line of Fort street, in accordance with
plans and specifications on file in the office of the Clerk of the Council of said city, for
constructing granite curbs.

Sec. 2. The Superintendent of Streets shall publish a notice of this proceeding each
day for five consecutive days after the publication of this resolution, in the Los Angeles
Evening Express, the official newspaper of the city, and shall post copies of said notice
along the line of said proposed improvement at a distance of not to exceed three hun-
dred feet apart, and if within ten days after the publication of said notice the property
owners along said street, amounting to one-half of the frontage thereof, shall file
with the Clerk a written objection against said improvement, then and in that
case said improvement shall not be proceeded with.

Sec. 3. If no remonstrance be filed, as hereinbefore provided, within the time
specified, the Council shall have jurisdiction to order said work proceeded with, and to
vy said street to be paved, and curbed in accordance with said plans and specifica-

ions.

Sec. 4, The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the ase of this resolution, and
shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Evening Express, and
thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force,

A REso.vuTion of the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles of their intention
to improve a portion of Second street.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

SEcTION 1. That the public interest and convenience require that Second street, in
said city, between Alameda street and Santa Fe street, and including all intersections of
streets, be graded, graveled and curbed; that it is the intention of the Councilof said City
of Los Angeles to order the following work to be done, to-wit:

(1) That Second street, in said city, from the east line of Alameda street to the west
line of Santa Fe street, be graded, graveled and curbed, in accordance with the plans and
aeons on file in the office of the Clerk of the Council, for making gravel streets

n said city.

(2) That a redwood curb be constructed along the line of roadway of said Second
street, from the east line of Alameda street to the west line of Santa Fe street, in accord-
ance with the plans and specification on file in the office of the Clerk of the Council of
said city, for constructing redwood curbs.

Sec. 2. The Superintendent of Streets shall publish a notice of this proceeding each
day for five consecutive days after the publication of this resolution, in the Los Angeles
Evening Express, the official newspaper of the we and shall post copies of said notice
along the line of said proposed improvement at a istance of not to exceed three hundred
feet apart.and if within ten davs after the publication of said notice the ieee
owners along said street, amounting to one-half of the frontage thereof, shall file wit!
the Clerk a written objection against said improvement, then and ift that case said
improvement shall not be proceeded with.

Src. 3. If no remonstrance be filed, as hereinbefore provided, within the time speci-
fied, the Council shall have jurisdiction to order said work proceeded with, and to order
said street to be graded, graveled and curbed in accordance with said plans and specifi-

_ cations.

Sec. 4, The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolution, and
shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Evening Express, and
thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council of the City
of Los Angeles at its meeting of July 2, A. D. 1888, by the following vote:

Ayes—Mesers. Barrett, Book, Bosbyshell, Chandler, Collins, Gibbs, Hanley, Hiller,
Mathews, Moriarty, Sinsavaugh, Teed and President Humphreys.

Noes—None.

RESOLUTION NO, 1049.
RESOLUTION OF INTENTION.

A Reso.ution of the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles of their intention to
improve a portion of Fort street.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

SEecTION 1. That the public interest and convenience require that Fort street,
in said city, between Temple street and Sixth street, and including all intersections
of streets, be paved and curbed; that it is the intention of the Council of said City of
Los Angeles to order the following work to be done, to-wit:

(1) That said Fort street, in said city, from the south line of Temple street to the
north line of Sixth street, be paved in accordance with plans and specifications on file
in the office of the Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles, for paving streets
in said city with broken rock and bituminous lime rock surface,

(2) That a granite curb be constructed along the line of roadway of said Fort street,
from the south line of Temple street to the north line of Sixth street, in accordance
with plans and specifications on file in the office of the Clerk of the Council of said city,
for constructing granite curbs, except as to that portion where a curb is already con-
structed, of granite or cement, satisfactory to the Superintendent of Streets.

Src. 2. The Superintendent of Streets shall publish a notice of this proceeding each
day for tive consecutive days after the publication of this resolution, in the Los Angeles
Evening Express, the official newspaper of the city, and shall post copies of said notice
along the line of said proposed improvement at a distance of not to exceed three hun-
dred feet apart, and if within ten days after the publication of said notice the property
owners along said street, amounting to one-half of the frontage thereof, shall file with
the Clerk a written objection against said improvement, then and in that case said
improvement shall not pe proceeded with.

Sec. 3. If no remonstrance be filed, as hereinbefore provided, within the time speci-
fied, the Council shall have jurisdiction to order said work to be proceeded with, and to
— said street to be paved and curbed, iu accordance with said plans and specifica-

ons,

Src. 4. ‘The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolution, and
shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Evening Express, and
thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

 

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles at its meeting of July 30, A. D. 1888, by the following vote: ,

Ayes—Messrs. Barrett, Book, Bosbyshell, Collins, Gibbs, Hanley, Lovell, Mathews,
Moriarty, Sinsabaugk, Teed and President Humphreys.

Noes—Mr. Chandler.
FREEMAN G. TEED,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Lus Angeles.

Approved this 2d day of August, A. D, 1888.
W. H. WORKMAN,
Mayor.

road, be and the same is hereby changea and established as follows: At the west line of
Waters street the grade shall be as now established, 226 30 feet above the datum plane
on the north corner, and 224.70 feet above the datum plane on the south corner; at a
point 200.00 feet west of the west line of Waters street the grade shall be 226.80 feet above
the datum plane on the north side, and 225,20 feet above the datum plane on the south
sides; at a point 400.00 feet west of the west line of Waters street the grade shall be
228.75 feet above the datum plane on the north side, and 227.75 feet above the datum plane
on the south side; ata point 450,00 feet west of the west line of Waters street the grade
shall be 229.00 feet above the datum plane on the north side, and 228.00 feet above the
datum plane on the south side; at the intersection with Edgeware road the grade shall
be as now established, 216.00 feet above the datum plane on the northeast corner, and
215.00 feet above the datum plane on the southeast corner.

Sec 2. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolution, and
cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Evening Express, and thereupon
and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council of the City
of Los Angeles at its meeting of September 3, A. D. 1888,

Evening Express, the official newspaper of the city, and shall post copies of said notice

RESOLUTION NO, 1159.
RESOLUTION OF INTENTION.

A RESOLUTION of the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles of their intention to
improve a portion of Third street.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles.

SEcTION 1. That the public interest and convenience require that Third street, in
said city, between Hewitt street and Santa Fe avenue, and including all intersections of
streets, be graded, graveled and curbed; that it isthe intention of the Council of said
City of Los Angeles to order the following work to be done, to-wit:

(1) That said Third street, in said city, from the east line of Hewitt street to the
west line of Santa Fe avenue, be graded, graveled and curbed in accordance with plans
and specifications on file in the office of the Clerk of the Council of the City of Los
Angeles, for making gravel streets in said city.

(2) That a redwood curb be constructed along the line of roadway of said Third
street, from the east line of Hewitt street to the west line of Santa Fe avenue, in accord-
ance with tbe plans and specifications on file in the office of the Clerk of the Council of
said city, for constructing redwood curbs.

Src. 2, The Superintendent of Streets shall publish a notice of this proceeding each
day for five consecutive days after the publication of this resolution, in the Los Angeles
Evening Express, the official newspaper of the city, and shall post copies of said notice
along the line of said proposed improvement at a distance of not to exceed three hundred
feet apart, and if within ten days after the publication of said notice the property own-
ers along said street, amounting to one-half of the frontage thereof, shall file with the
Clerk a written objection against said improvement, then and in that case said im-
provement shall not be proceeded with.

Sec. 3. Jf no remonstrance be filed, as hereinbefore provided, within the time speci-
fied, tue Council shall have jurisdiction to order said work proceeded with, and to order
= street to be graded, graveled and curbed in accordance with said plans and specifi-
cations.

Sec. 4, The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolution, and
shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Evening Express, and
thereupon and thereafter it shajl take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council of the City
of Los Angeles at its meeting of October 1, A. D. 1888, by the following vote:

Ayes—Messrs. Book, Chandler, Gibbs, Hanley, Mathews, Sinsabaugh, Teed and Presi-
dent Humphreys.

Noes—None,
FREEMAN G. TEED,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 5th day of October, A. D, 1888.
W. H. WORKMAN,

RESOLUTION OF INTENTION.

A Reso_vuTion of the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles of their intention to
improve a portion of Fort street.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1. That the public interest and convenience require that Fort street, in
said city, between the south line of Temple street and a point 10 feet south of the center

 
=== p-639 ===
620 RESOLUTIONS OF THE

line of Fourth street, and including all intersections of streets, be sewered; and it is
pe, eventos of the Council of said City of Los Angeles to order the following work to
be done, to-wit:

(1) That said Fort street, in said city, from the south line of Temple street to a point
10 feet south of the center line of Fourth street, be sewered, in accordance with plans
and specifications on file in the office of the Citv Surveyor of the City of Los Angeles, for
the laying down and construction of vitrified clay pipe sewers; that portion of said sewer
between the south line of Temple street and a point 10 feet south of the center line of
First street. a distance of 1,000 feet, shall be built of pipe having a clear inside diameter
of 10 inches, and that portion between a point 10 feet south of the center line of First
street and a point 10 feet south of the center line of Fourth street, a distance of 1,866 feet,
shall be built of pipe having a clear inside diameter of 12 inches.

(2) That brick manholes be constructed along the line of said sewer, from the south
line of Temple street to its termination, 10 feet south of the center Jine of Fourth street,
at each street intersection; said manholes to be constructed in accordance with plans an
specifications on file in the office of the City Surveyor.

Src. 2. -The Superintendent of Streets shall publish a notice of this proceeding each
day for tive consecutive days after the publication of this resolution, in the Los Angeles
Evening Express, the official newspaper of the city, and shall post copies of said notice
along the line of said proposed improvement at a distance of not to exceed three hun-
dred feet apart, and if within ten days after the publication of said notice the property
owners along said street, amounting to one-half of the frontage thereof, shall file with
the Clerk a written objection against said improvement, then and in that case said
improvement shall not pe proceeded with.

Sec. 3. If no remonstrance be filed, as hereinbefore provided, within the time speci-
fied, the Council shall have jurisdiction to order said work to be proceeded with, and to
order said street to be sewered, in accordance with said plans,and specifications.

Src. 4. ‘The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolution, and
shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Evening Express, and
thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles at its meeting of October 8, A. D. 1888, by the following vote:

Ayes—Messrs. Book, Chandler, Cohn, Collins, Gibbs, Hanley, Hiller, Mathews,
Moriarty and President Humphreys.

Noes—None.

be sewered, in accordance with plans and specifications on file in the office of the City
Surveyor of the City of Los Angeles, for the laying down and construction of vitrified —
clay pipe sewers. Said sewer throughout its entire length shall be buili of pipe having a
clear inside diameter of eighteen (18) inches. ¥

Sec. 2. The Superintendent of Streets shall publish a notice of this proceeding each

along the line of said proposed improvement at a distance of not to exceed three hundred

That said Seventh street, in said city, from the east line of Pearl street to a point 980

office of the City Surveyor of the City of Los Angeles, for the Jaying down and con-
struction of vitrified clay pipe sewers, and that said sewer shall have a clear inside

fied, the Council shall have jurisdiction to order said work to be proceeded with, and to

thereupon and thereafter it shail take effect and be in force. °

Sec. 2. The Clerk of this Council is hereby directed to — conspicuously for five
days, on or near the Council Chamber door, notice hereof, and is also directed to publish
such notice in the Los Angeles Daily Herald, a newspaper published and circulated
daily in this city, for five days, as often as said newspaper is issued therein.

RESOLUTION NO. 1278.
RESOLUTION OF INTENTION.

A SOLUTION of the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles of their intention to
onstruct a sewer along New Main street.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

SEcTION 1, Thatthe public interest and convenience require that a public sewer
be constructed a New Main street, in said city, between Alameda street and Wilbardt
street, and across all intersections of streets, and that it is the intention of the Council
of said City of Los Angeles to order the following work to be done, to-wit:

That a ape sewer shall be constructed along New Main street, in said city, from
the center line of Wilhardt street to the intersection of the present sewer in Alameda
street, in accordance with the plans and specifications on file in the office of the Clerk
of the Council of the City of Los Angeles. The size of said sewer shall be twelve (12)
inches inside diameter from its connection with the Alameda-street sewer to the center
line of Elmira street, and ten (10) inches inside diameter from center line of Elmira
street to the center line of Wilhardt street. The material used for constructing said
sewer shall be the best quality of salt-glazed vitrified pipe.

Sec, 2. The Superintendent of Streets shall publish a notice of this proceeding each
day for tive consecutive days after the publication of this resolution, in the Los Angeles
Daily Herald, the official newspaper of the city, and shall post copies of said notice
along the line of said proposed improvement at a distance of not to exceed three hundred
feet apart, and if within ten davs after the publication of said notice the property own-
ers along said street, amounting to one-half of the frontage thereof, shall file with the
Clerk a written objection against said improvement, then and in that case the Council
shall hear and determine said objections as provided by law.

Sec. 3. If no remonstrance be filed, as hereinbefore provided, within the time speci-
fied, the Council shall have jurisdiction to order said work proceeded with, and to order
said sewer to be constructed in accordance with said plans and specifications.

Sec. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolution, and
shall cause tbe same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily Herald, and there-
upon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles at its meeting of December 24, A. D. 1888, by the following vote:

Ayes—Messrs. Barrett, Earl, Ford, Hanley, McNally, Moriarty, Shafer, Sinsabaugh,
Threlkeld and President Kuhrts.

Noes—None.
FREEMAN G. TFED,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 29th day of December, A. D. 1885.
JOHN BRYSON, SR.,

Mayor.
Published December 31, 1888.

RESOLUTION NO. 1278.

A RESOLUTION of the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles relative to the
submission of the proposed charter to the Legislature of the State of California.

WHEREAS, On the 31st day of May, A. D. 1888, a special election was held in the City

of Los Angeles, at which fifteen freeholders were elected to prepare and propose a charter

for the City of Los Angeles; and

WHEREAS, On the 238d day of August, A. D. 1888, said freeholders so elected duly
returned a proposed charter for said City of Los Angeles, signed iu dupiicate by the
entire board, one copy thereof to the Mayor of said city, and the other to the Recorder
of Deeds of the County of Los Angeles; and :

Wuereas Said proposed charter was duly published in two daily papers of general
circulation, in said city, to-wit, the Evening Express and Daily Tribune, for a period of
twenty days (Sundays excepted); said publication in each instance commencing within
twenty days after the completion of said charter; and ;

WHEREAS, On the 20th day of October, 1888, a special election was held, at which the
proposed charter was submitted to the qualified electors of the City of Los Angeles; and

WHEREAS, On the 22d day of October, 1888, the Council of the City of Los Angeles
duly canvassed the returns of said election, and deciared the result to be as follows: In
favor of said charter, 2,642 votes; against said charter, 1,890; majority in favor of said
charter, 752 votes; and that said charter was duly ratified by a majority of the qualified
electors voting at said election; and

WHEREAS, Said charter must be submitted tothe Legislature of the State of California
for its approval or rejection as a whole; now, therefore,

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

SrcTION 1, That the Hon. Stephen M. White, Senator from the Thirty-eighth Sena-
torial District of California, in which district is included the City of Los Angeles, and
=== p-711 ===
 

692 " RESOLUTIONS OF THE

the Hon. J. M. Damron, Representative from the Seventy-seventh Assembly District of
said State, said district being composed wholly of the City of Los angeles, be and a
hereby‘requested to submit said proposed charter to the Legislature of the State of Ca c
fornia, which will convene at Sacramento, on Monday, the 7th day of January, 1889, a

the earliest possible moment, and that they be and are hereby further requested to use
every honorable endeavor to have said charter approved by the Legislature of the State

of California.

Sec. 2. The Clerk of the Council is hereby instructed and directed to forward to the
honorable Senator and Representative above named certified copies of this resolution
immediately upon its approval and publication,

SEc.3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolution, and
shall cause tne same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily Herald, and there-
upon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that at a meeting of the Council of the City of Los Angeles held
Monday, December 31, the foregoing resolution was adopted.

FREEMAN G. TEED,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 31st day of December, A. D. 1888.

JOHN BRYSON, SR.,
Mayor.
